question.text: A Section 8 Company, once registered under the Companies Act 2013, enjoys which of the following privileges?

answer.text: All privileges of a limited company WITHOUT the need to add 'Pvt. Ltd.' to its name, provided profits are applied towards its objects
Automatic tax exemption under Section 11 without separate 12AB registration
Exemption from filing annual returns with the RoC

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Table 1.1 / Ch 1.3.1, a Section 8 Company enjoys all the privileges of a limited company without needing to add 'Pvt. Ltd.' to its name, conditional on profits being applied to its objects and no dividend distribution to members. **The Trap:** Option B is wrong — 12AB registration is separate and not automatic. Option C is wrong — Section 8 Companies must file annual returns with RoC. Option D is wrong — FCRA requires separate registration with MHA. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-links to Ch 11 (Key Regulations) and III-A (Compliance) for RoC filings. SIAs must not conflate 'Section 8 status' with 'tax exemption' or 'FCRA clearance'. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Section 8 status is the legal form ONLY. Tax exemption (12AB), donor deduction (80G), and foreign contribution (FCRA) are three separate registrations — verify each independently on engagement.
